title: Warfarin After Seven Decades: Persistent Value and the Contemporary Role of Vitamin K Antagonism.
authors: Weverton Ferreira Leite; Wilma Noia Ribeiro; Rui Manuel Dos Santos Povoa; Dirceu Rodrigues de Almeida; Daniela Fernanda Alli Hemerly; Braulio Luna Filho; Valdir Ambrosio Moises; Jose Antonio Franchini Ramires
abstract: Warfarin is one of the most enduring drugs in cardiovascular medicine. Although direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) have transformed anticoagulation, especially in atrial fibrillation (AF) eligible for DOAC therapy, their success cannot be extrapolated to every thrombotic substrate. This review examines the contemporary boundaries of warfarin and vitamin K antagonist (VKA) therapy. Mechanical heart valves remain the clearest setting in which lifelong international normalized ratio (INR)-guided VKA therapy is required; randomized attempts to substitute dabigatran or apixaban have failed. In rheumatic heart disease-associated AF, INVICTUS favored VKA therapy over rivaroxaban, supporting the VKA class rather than warfarin specifically. High-risk thrombotic antiphospholipid syndrome, particularly triple-positive disease, is another VKA-preferred setting. Left ventricular thrombus (LVT) occupies an evolving position in which warfarin remains established, while randomized evidence supports rivaroxaban as a potential alternative in selected acute post-myocardial infarction LVT. Pregnancy with mechanical valves requires dynamic maternal-fetal risk balancing, whereas advanced chronic kidney disease and dialysis represent areas of uncertainty rather than intrinsic indications for warfarin. The global relevance of warfarin also depends on total anticoagulation burden, including INR monitoring, travel, treatment continuity, quality of anticoagulation, and reversal capacity. The persistence of VKA efficacy in selected highly thrombogenic environments raises a biologically plausible hypothesis that broader suppression of vitamin K-dependent factors may matter, but this mechanism is not established by clinical trials. Contemporary anticoagulation should therefore be substrate-centered: VKA therapy remains necessary in some conditions, preferred in others, increasingly replaceable in several, and uncertain in a few.

title: Digoxin Revisited: An Updated Review in the Light of Recent Trials.
authors: Muhammad Saad; Muhammad Abdullah; Ankit Yelamarthy; Krystal John; Abbas Hayat Mallick; Behram Khan; Hassan Tahir; Rajan Krishnamani
abstract: Isolated from Digitalis species following William Withering's 1785 work on foxglove, digoxin inhibits myocardial Na+/K+-ATPase, raising intracellular calcium and vagal tone to produce inotropic, rate-controlling, and neurohormonal-deactivating effects. The foundational DIG trial (1997) showed no mortality benefit but reduced heart failure hospitalizations, prompting a progressive guideline downgrade. Three decades later, DIGIT-HF (2025, digitoxin) and DECISION (2026, low dose digoxin) retested cardiac glycosides atop modern four pillar guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT). DIGIT-HF significantly reduced the composite of death or worsening heart failure (hazard ratio (HR), 0.82), while DECISION showed a numerical but nonsignificant benefit. A pooled meta-analysis of DIG, DIGIT-HF, and DECISION (9,013 patients) confirmed a consistent 15% reduction in worsening heart failure events across three decades of changing background therapy, without a significant mortality effect. The Dig-RHD trial addressed an unstudied population: symptomatic rheumatic heart disease (RHD), a chronic valvular heart disease that results from permanent damage to cardiac valves due to group A streptococcal infection. RHD affects roughly 40 million people and causes approximately 300,000 deaths annually, disproportionately in low- and middle-income countries. In 1,769 patients randomized across 12 Indian centers, digoxin significantly reduced the composite of death or new-onset/worsening heart failure (31.4% vs. 35.5%; HR, 0.82; 95% confidence interval (CI), 0.70 to 0.97; P = 0.02), with greater benefit in atrial fibrillation, women, and patients with low body mass index (BMI), and a number needed to treat of approximately 14 over 2 years. Digoxin is not a mortality-reducing drug, but pooled contemporary evidence establishes it as a reproducible, low-cost tool for reducing heart failure events, now supported for the first time by high-quality randomized data in RHD, a population with substantial global burden and no prior evidence-based medical therapy. These findings warrant reconsideration of digoxin's guideline status and development of RHD-specific recommendations.

title: Translational maturity of artificial intelligence-enabled electrocardiography varies across cardiovascular diseases.
authors: Huanhuan Chen; Jingjuan Huang; Xumin Hou
abstract: Electrocardiography is a widely available and low-cost cardiovascular test, and artificial intelligence-enabled electrocardiography (AI-ECG) can identify latent electrical phenotypes beyond conventional interpretation. However, high retrospective discrimination does not necessarily translate into clinically reliable or actionable benefit. This critical narrative review evaluates the translational maturity of AI-ECG across arrhythmias, acute myocardial infarction, heart failure, valvular heart disease, hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, and cardiac amyloidosis. PubMed, IEEE Xplore, and Web of Science were searched from January 1, 2022, through July 10, 2026, with earlier landmark studies added by backward citation tracking. Seventy-seven publications informed the review. Evidence was appraised using five clinically oriented criteria: intended use, reference-standard reliability, external validation and transportability, clinical actionability, and effects on workflow or patient outcomes. AI-ECG has progressed furthest in ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction triage and reduced-left-ventricular-ejection-fraction screening, where prospective or randomized studies have demonstrated workflow or diagnostic-yield benefits, whereas acute myocardial infarction rule-out has reached prospective multicenter diagnostic validation. Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy screening has also advanced through international validation and prospective implementation. By contrast, occlusion myocardial infarction detection, prediction of occult or future atrial fibrillation, valvular heart disease, heart failure with preserved ejection fraction, long-term heart-failure prediction, and cardiac amyloidosis remain primarily validation-stage or risk-enrichment applications. Across domains, broader adoption is constrained by label quality, calibration, transportability, operating-threshold selection, and limited patient-outcome evidence. AI-ECG is therefore best positioned as clinician-supervised decision support linked to explicit downstream testing and care pathways.

title: Regional Divergence in Infective Endocarditis Prophylaxis: A Multi-center Analysis of Clinical Practice vs. International Guidelines from the Pan Arab Congenital Heart Disease Association (PACHDA).
authors: Ali Al Akhfash; Nagib Dahdah; Milad El-Segaier
abstract: Current infective endocarditis (IE) prophylaxis guidelines recommend a restrictive approach, excluding low-risk lesions such as patent ductus arteriosus, isolated ventricular septal defect, and valvular stenosis. In many countries, delayed cardiac defect repair and a high prevalence of dental disease may create a distinct risk profile that warrants further investigation. The Pan Arab Congenital Heart Disease Association (PACHDA) conducted a multinational cross-sectional online survey targeting cardiovascular specialists to evaluate perceptions of IE prophylaxis guidelines, adherence patterns, and the influence of oral health and socioeconomic factors on clinical decision-making. Statistical analyses included Spearman rank correlation, Chi-square testing, Fisher's exact test, and qualitative thematic synthesis. The questionnaire was completed by 72 specialists, of whom only 25% reported strict adherence to restrictive international guidelines for isolated simple congenital heart defects. Respondents who identified socioeconomic barriers (e.g., poverty and limited access to dental care) as a primary concern were more likely to deviate from restrictive guideline recommendations than their peers (83.7% vs. 41.4%; p = 0.001). Clinicians with higher IE case exposure (> 5 IE cases in the preceding 5 years) also demonstrated significantly greater rates of guideline deviation (p = 0.047). Fewer than 50% of respondents considered current AHA/ESC guidelines "fit for purpose" in their local practice. Many cardiovascular specialists across the Arab/MENA region perceive current international IE prophylaxis recommendations as insufficiently reflective of local clinical and socioeconomic realities. However, these findings represent clinician perceptions and practice patterns rather than patient-level outcomes and should therefore be considered hypothesis-generating. The observed divergence between guideline recommendations and clinical practice highlights the need for regional epidemiological and outcome-based studies to determine whether local factors influence IE risk and whether adaptation of current prophylaxis strategies is warranted.

title: Remodeling of Failed Pulmonary Valve Autografts After the Ross Procedure.
authors: Vaclav Stejskal; Tereza Sokolova; Jakub Sagat; Barbora Vasova; Lucia Hrnciarova; Petr Smolak
abstract: The Ross procedure utilizes a pulmonary autograft for aortic valve replacement, but late autograft failure remains a clinical challenge. In this exploratory study, we characterized structural alterations in failed pulmonary autografts using digital morphometric analysis. Five autografts explanted because of regurgitation were compared with six autopsy control pulmonary valves using special stains and alpha-smooth muscle actin immunohistochemistry. One histologically most affected section per valve was evaluated using QuPath. Failed autografts showed leaflet thickening, elastosis, fibrosis, and myxomatous matrix accumulation. Compared with controls, autografts had greater maximum leaflet thickness (1.540 vs. 0.447 mm; P = 0.004), cross-sectional area (8.730 vs. 3.045 mm²; P = 0.004), α-SMA-positive area (0.707 vs. 0.046 mm²; P = 0.008), and α-SMA-positive area fraction (0.069 vs. 0.016; P = 0.017). The findings demonstrate extracellular matrix alterations and increased α-SMA immunoreactivity in hotspot regions, suggesting a myxomatous-like remodeling pattern.

title: Cat eye syndrome chromosome region, candidate 1 is a novel prognostic biomarker in hypertrophic cardiomyopathy.
authors: Yu Zhang; Fangfang Wan; Chen Li; Bo Wang; Mo Zhang; Minjie Lu; Lianming Kang; Liwen Liu; Jizheng Wang; Lei Song
abstract: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) exhibits great prognostic heterogeneity, necessitating the identification of high-risk patients for timely treatment. This study aimed to find novel prognostic biomarkers directly from diseased cardiac tissue to improve risk stratification of HCM. We utilized a myocardial transcriptome discovery cohort (n = 246; median follow-up 6.8 years) alongside two independent plasma validation cohorts (Beijing, n = 1,238; follow-up 2.5 years; Xi'an, n = 402; follow-up 4.8 years). The primary and secondary endpoints were cardiovascular death and sudden cardiac death (SCD), respectively. In the discovery cohort, myocardial expression of CECR1 (cat eye syndrome chromosome region, candidate 1, also known as ADA2, Adenosine Deaminase 2) demonstrated the strongest association with cardiovascular death (P = 9.6 × 10-5). Plasma CECR1 levels correlated modestly but significantly with myocardial expression. In the Beijing validation cohort, decreased plasma CECR1 predicted increased risks of cardiovascular death (adjusted hazard ratio (HR) 3.731, P < 0.001) and SCD (adjusted HR 7.398, P < 0.001), with areas under the curves (AUCs) of 0.720 and 0.798, respectively. These findings were replicated in the Xi'an validation cohort. Integrating plasma CECR1 into the HCM Risk-SCD model significantly enhanced its predictive performance, increasing the AUC from 0.723 to 0.845 (P = 0.031) in the Beijing validation cohort and consistently improving it from 0.600 to 0.781 (P = 0.018) in the Xi'an validation cohort. In conclusion, CECR1 represents a novel prognostic biomarker of HCM. Measurement of CECR1 may improve risk stratification by facilitating the identification of individuals at higher risk of cardiovascular mortality. CECR1 assessment may provide additional information for SCD risk evaluation and support clinical decision-making regarding implantable cardioverter-defibrillator therapy.

title: Outcomes of Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement in the Middle East and North Africa: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
authors: Mohammad-Mahdi Bastan; Sahand Siami; Fatemeh Jodeiri; Sina Kazemian; Mandana Ebrahimzade; Niloofar Seighali; Saba Maleki; Nazanin Anaraki; Magdy Abdelhamid; Saif-El-Dean Abdel-Rahman; Kaveh Hosseini
journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
abstract:
Data on transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) outcomes in the Middle East and North Africa region are limited. We synthesized available evidence on post-TAVR clinical outcomes in the Middle East and North Africa region.
We systematically searched PubMed, Embase, and Scopus from inception through May 2025 for studies reporting TAVR outcomes in this region. Outcomes included device success, all-cause death, cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction, stroke, new-onset atrial fibrillation, moderate to severe paravalvular leak, and permanent pacemaker implantation. Overall incidence rates were pooled via Poisson analysis and reported per 100 person-years with 95% CIs.
Forty-eight studies encompassing 7331 patients (mean age, 76.9±8.5 years; 52.4% women) were included. Pooled device success rate was 96.4% (95% CI, 95.8%-97.0%). At latest follow-up, pooled incidence rates per 100 person-years were 13.7 for all-cause death (95% CI, 12.9-14.6), 4.8 for cardiovascular death (95% CI, 4.1-5.7), 1.0 for myocardial infarction (95% CI, 0.7-1.4), 1.6 for stroke (95% CI, 1.3-1.9), 2.7 for moderate to severe paravalvular leak (95% CI, 2.2-3.4), 6.5 for new-onset atrial fibrillation (95% CI, 5.5-7.7), and 10.0 for permanent pacemaker implantation (95% CI, 9.2-10.9). Post hoc exploratory meta-regression identified significant study-level modifying effects, with higher mean age and greater use of first-generation versus second-generation valves associated with higher overall all-cause mortality incidence following TAVR. Certainty of evidence was low or very low across all outcomes.
TAVR in the Middle East and North Africa region was associated with high device success rate and relatively low cardiovascular death. Permanent pacemaker implantation was the most prevalent post-TAVR complication. Further studies are warranted to optimize TAVR practice in this region.

title: Comparison of 1-year costs of commercially insured patients with severe aortic stenosis undergoing surgical vs. transcatheter aortic valve replacement.
authors: Suzanne J Baron; Benjamin Z Galper; Marcella A Kelley; Soumya G Chikermane; Shannon M E Murphy
abstract:
Patients with aortic stenosis (AS) have been shown to have lower costs at 1 year with transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) compared with surgical aortic valve replacement (SAVR) in a Medicare population. The difference in costs between TAVR and SAVR in commercially insured patients with AS in the United States is unknown.
Using the Optum claims database, AS patients receiving either TAVR or SAVR between 3/2019 and 9/2022 were identified. Patients were categorized into low, intermediate or high strata using the Hospital Frailty Risk Score (HFRS). The primary outcome was total 1-year cost, defined as the sum of index AVR hospitalization and 1-year follow-up costs. Risk-adjusted generalized linear models were used to assess the difference in the costs between TAVR and SAVR.
3,623 patients (952 TAVR; 2,671 SAVR) were identified. TAVR patients had lower index hospitalization costs compared with SAVR patients across all HFRS strata (cost difference for low: $39,312, p < 0.01; intermediate: $42,006, p < 0.01; high: $39,431, p = 0.03). Cumulative costs through one year were significantly lower with TAVR in the low and intermediate HFRS strata (cost difference for low: $32,116, p < 0.01; intermediate $40,905, p < 0.01) and numerically lower in the high HFRS stratum (cost difference: $35,881, p = 0.15). When the analysis was restricted to isolated AVR, the 1-year difference was no longer significant in the low and intermediate HFRS strata ($8,064 and $11,314, respectively) and was numerically reversed in the high HFRS stratum (-$28,804).
In a commercial payor population of real-world patients with AS, TAVR was associated with lower standardized index hospitalization costs across all HFRS strata and lower standardized 1-year costs in the low and intermediate HFRS strata. These findings demonstrate that baseline frailty and procedural scope are critical determinants of short and intermediate-term cost differences between TAVR and SAVR for the treatment of AS in commercial populations.

title: Clustering of Cardiovascular Risk Factors in Midlife Forms Trajectories That Affect Heart Aging Biomarker and Incidence of Cardiovascular Disease.
authors: Arya Panthalanickal Vijayakumar; Tom Wilsgaard; Henrik Schirmer; Haakon Lindekleiv; Zachi I Attia; Francisco Lopez-Jimenez; David A Leon; Olena Iakunchykova
abstract:
To (1) identify multivariable longitudinal midlife patterns of systolic and diastolic blood pressure, body mass index, and non-high density lipoprotein cholesterol and (2) assess whether electrocardiogram derived heart age acceleration (δ-age) mediates their associations with incident myocardial infarction (MI), stroke, and all-cause mortality.
We analyzed 5244 participants from the observational cohort study, the Tromsø Study, who were free of MI or stroke at baseline (Tromsø7, 2015-2016) and attended at least 3 surveys (Tromsø3-7, 1986-2016). Age-standardized risk factor z-scores were modeled with quadratic B-splines and grouped using K-means clustering to identify joint multivariable life-course risk profiles. δ-Age was derived from 12-lead electrocardiograms using a validated neural network. Natural-effects models decomposed hazard ratios between clusters and clinical events (follow-up to 2021) into direct and δ-age mediated components.
Four distinct clusters were identified: stable low-risk (cluster 1, n=1604, 30.6%), dyslipidemia (cluster 2, n=1340, 25.6%), hypertension (cluster 3, n=1476, 28.1%), and high-risk trajectory (cluster 4, n=824, 15.7%). Each 1-SD increment in δ-age was associated with 27% to 30% of excess MI, stroke, and death, independent of age and sex. Clusters 3 and 4 carried the greatest excess risk of clinical events, whereas mediation by δ-age was modest (4%-8% of total effect for MI and stroke) and not statistically significant.
Joint multivariable life-course clustering of conventional risk factors identified clinically distinct long-term cardiovascular risk phenotypes. Although δ-age adds independent prognostic information, it explained little of the excess risk associated with chronic hypertension, dyslipidemia, or obesity, indicating it functions primarily as a parallel marker and not a causal mediator.

title: Patient attitudes toward artificial intelligence-driven dermatology.
authors: Natalie Bourand; Mackenzie Vick; Amanda P Siegel; Maria M Tsoukas; Kamran Avanaki
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) systems are increasingly being developed for dermatology, but the conditions under which patients trust these tools remain poorly characterized. This Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses-guided systematic narrative review synthesizes peer-reviewed empirical studies, published from January 1, 2015 through July 7, 2026, that directly assessed patient or public attitudes toward AI in dermatologic diagnosis, skin-cancer screening, image sharing, teledermatology image-quality support, and related patient-facing workflows. Eligible evidence included qualitative interviews and focus groups, surveys, preference/conjoint or vignette experiments, and early clinical deployments. Twenty studies met the inclusion criteria using the review framework. Across study designs, patients expressed conditional support for dermatology AI but consistently favored dermatologist-supervised AI over autonomous AI, especially for high-stakes diagnostic decisions. Trust was strengthened by visible clinician accountability, clear explanations of AI outputs and uncertainty, privacy safeguards, transparent data use, and evidence that performance is reliable across skin tone and diagnosis. Trust declined when AI was framed as replacing clinicians, when image governance was unclear, or when unequal performance was perceived. These findings support a model of augmented intelligence: dermatology AI should serve the clinical relationship; be subject to human oversight; and be evaluated and reported stratified by skin tone, diagnosis, and care context.

title: HiCP2GAN: a plug and play foundation model-based GAN for Hi-C enhancement.
authors: Samuel Olowofila; Oluwatosin Oluwadare
abstract: The 3D organization of chromatin shapes gene regulation and cellular function, and Hi-C has become the primary technique for mapping chromatin interactions genome-wide. However, high-resolution data remain costly and scarce, leaving many studies with sparse contact maps that limit downstream analysis. Deep learning methods, especially generative adversarial networks (GANs), have shown promise for enhancing low-resolution Hi-C data, but most existing GAN-based approaches rely on custom discriminators trained from scratch, which can yield unstable training and limited generalization. Hi-C foundation models pretrained on large-scale data capture rich, transferable representations of chromatin structure, yet their use as discriminators within adversarial enhancement frameworks had not been explored. We introduce HiCP2GAN, a plug-and-play GAN that employs a pretrained Vision Transformer-based Hi-C foundation model as its discriminator. The discriminator was pretrained on 118 million Hi-C patches across diverse species and cell types, providing biologically meaningful gradients for adversarial supervision. The framework is generator-agnostic: any compatible Hi-C resolution enhancement architecture can serve as the generator, enabling fair comparison across methods. The encoder phase of the foundation model was adapted as a discriminator backbone, finetuning the first few layers from the input while freezing the deeper transformer layers to preserve pretrained knowledge while allowing task-specific adaptation. Experiments across various cell lines show that HiCP2GAN outperforms traditional GAN-based methods in most settings and improves the reconstruction quality and biological reproducibility of existing Hi-C enhancement models in most evaluated cases. HiCP2GAN is publicly available at https://github.com/OluwadareLab/HiCP2GAN.

title: AxialTAD: an axial contrast architecture for TAD boundary prediction from Hi-C.
authors: Woo-Young Choi; Je-Keun Rhee
abstract: Topologically associating domains (TADs) are fundamental units of 3D chromatin organization, and accurate identification of TAD boundaries from Hi-C contact matrices remains an active challenge. Recent deep learning approaches have advanced substantially, but these rely on increasingly large architectures, raising the question of how much of this capacity boundary-centric analysis requires. Here we propose AxialTAD, a compact deep learning model centered on an Axial Contrast Module (ACM) that explicitly encodes directional contrast in contact intensity along the row and column axes of local Hi-C patches, an operator aligned with the geometric signature of TAD boundaries. Evaluated on four human cell lines (GM12878, HeLa-S3, IMR-90, K562) within cell lines and under leave-one-cell-out generalization, AxialTAD performed comparably with a recent convolutional neural network (CNN)+Transformer baseline (deepTAD) while using 76%-80% fewer trainable parameters (113K-137K versus 571K). A parameter-matched conventional CNN achieved similar F1 to AxialTAD in the human 25 kb experiments. When trained and evaluated within each of two mouse datasets, AxialTAD outperformed both this control and deepTAD. Orthogonal validation against CTCF and cohesin ChIP-seq supported the biological plausibility of the predicted boundaries. These results indicate that, within the range of architectures examined, a large architecture is not necessary to reach this level of boundary prediction.

title: Unit-Area Optimized Flexible Triboelectric Nanogenerators for High-Performance Human Motion Sensing With Deep Learning.
authors: Jeyun Lee; Seungbeom Kim; Agha Aamir Jan; Seok Kim
abstract: Triboelectric nanogenerators (TENGs) have garnered significant attention as self-powered energy harvesters and sensors, yet their performance critically depends on structural design and material engineering. In this work, we introduce a structured TENG designed with the concept of unit-area to maximize contact efficiency by minimizing mechanical interference between neighboring structures. Synergistically, barium titanate (BaTiO3) nanoparticles were incorporated into the elastomer matrix to enhance the dielectric constant and surface charge density. Based on this approach, unit-area-based TENGs (UA-TENGs) with various geometries were comprehensively evaluated through computational analysis and experimental validation. The results reveal that smaller structures enable more effective contact, while dome structures exhibit superior output compared to pyramid structures. Quantitatively, the optimized dome-structured UA-TENG with the BaTiO3 composite achieves a power density of 18 W/m2, a maximum voltage of 254 V, and enhanced pressure sensitivities. The device successfully powered 127 LEDs and operated small electronics. Furthermore, the UA-TENG demonstrated excellent performance in detecting biomechanical signals. Integration into a smart glove enabled real-time gesture recognition, where a convolutional neural network accurately classified five distinct hand motions to achieve reliable wireless drone control. These results demonstrate the broad application prospects of the UA-TENG in wearable energy supply, intelligent sensing, and human-machine interaction.

title: AI-Assisted Analysis of Clinical Trials to Identify Failed Drugs for Revival via Drug Delivery Technologies.
authors: Nianwu Wang; Rui Zhang; Hong-Bo Pang
abstract: Numerous drug candidates showed great promise in experimental and preclinical investigations but failed in clinical trials. One cause to this problem may be nonspecific drug biodistribution, leading to adverse effects in healthy organs. Drug delivery technologies are developed to overcome this exact problem by navigating drugs more selectively to the disease sites. Therefore, they hold the promise to revive at least some failed drugs. However, it is challenging to identify such candidates revivable by drug delivery: first, there lacks systemic survey and documentation of drug biodistribution in patients during the trials; second, clinical trial results, especially the failed ones, are often reported in unstructured and/or inconsistent language. Here, we harnessed the recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI) agents and large language models (LLMs) to tackle with the second problem. An OpenAI-based framework was developed to systemically analyze terminated trials on ClinicalTrials.gov. This framework integrated structured extraction of clinical trial information, disease-site inference with evaluation based on predefined screening criteria, which is unwanted biodistribution (UB failure) reflected by the difference in the anatomical locations between adverse effects and targeted diseases. We also paired this with the analysis of drug types and physicochemical properties (e.g. molecular weight and hydrophobicity). Using a validation set, the model achieved accuracies of 89.69% for UB failure classification, 91.75% for small molecule drug classification, and 88.66% for hydrophobicity classification. We then applied this analysis to all terminated ClinicalTrials.gov trials, which identified 817 trials possibly failed due to UB, and top ten small molecule drugs likely suitable for our peptide-guided delivery platform. Overall, this study may provide a new direction to apply AI technologies for drug development, and inspire future investigations of clinical reports and public information from the perspective of delivery technology applications.

title: Epistemic uncertainty as a diagnostic probe for deep learning Hamiltonians.
authors: Tianhao Su; Zeyun Gao; Shunbo Hu; Tong-Yi Zhang
abstract: The reliability of deep learning models for Hamiltonian prediction remains poorly understood, limiting their deployment in computational materials discovery workflows. Although these models offer an efficient alternative to density functional theory (DFT), they are vulnerable to producing confident but incorrect predictions when applied beyond their training distribution. Here, we systematically quantify the applicability domain of Hamiltonian prediction models using ensemble variance as a built-in uncertainty metric. Using bilayer and twisted bilayer graphene as well-controlled testbeds, we demonstrate that ensemble variance (Δσ) exhibits strong linear correlation with mean absolute error (MAE) in all structural modulations (Pearson correlation coefficient >0.91), which allows it to serve as a DFT-free reliability indicator. The model maintains high accuracy (MAE < 2.5 meV) within limited structural perturbations: uniaxial strain from to 5%, interlayer distance from 2.95 to 3.75 Å, and length of the C-C bond from 1.41 to 1.44 Å. We further evaluated transfer to other carbon allotropes and obtained MAE values of 13.02 meV for graphite (Δσ = 3.93 meV), 13.99 meV for twisted graphite (Δσ = 3.94 meV), 15.80 meV for carbon nanotubes (Δσ = 4.09 meV), and 39.45 meV for fullerenes (Δσ = 10.85 meV). These results establish ensemble variance as a practical reliability indicator and underscore the critical need for pre-establishing applicability boundaries before deploying machine learning models in computational research workflows.

title: YOLOv11-based segmentation of vitiligo lesions using standardized clinical photography.
authors: Sania Tanvir; Sidra Abid Syed; Zia Mohyuddin; Abdul Moid Khan; Jahanzeb Sheikh; Nimra Mehmood; Tan Tian Swee; Maheza Irna Muhammad Binti Salem
abstract:
To develop and validate a YOLOv11-based deep learning framework that automatically segments vitiligo lesions in standardized clinical photographs captured under controlled conditions, enabling reproducible lesion quantification across longitudinal visits.
Standardized photographs from 18 patients were acquired at baseline, 3 months, and 6 months under controlled imaging conditions, including fixed lighting, camera settings, and color calibration. Images underwent preprocessing involving resizing, color and illumination normalization, noise reduction, and geometric standardization. Expert dermatologists generated binary lesion masks that were used as ground truth for training a one-stage YOLOv11 segmentation model. Model performance was evaluated using patient-wise data splits and 5-fold cross-validation.
The proposed model achieved 95 % accuracy, 92 % precision, 89 % recall, 90 % F1-score, with mAP@0.5 values of 0.878 (bounding box) and 0.892 (mask) from precision-recall analysis. Qualitative review indicated consistent segmentation quality across follow-up visits and moderate illumination variations, though formally stratified quantitative analysis by visit was not performed in this study. Visual assessment demonstrated close agreement between predicted and expert-annotated lesion boundaries, with minor under-segmentation observed mainly in low-contrast peripheral regions.
Standardized clinical photography combined with a YOLOv11-based segmentation framework enables reliable vitiligo lesion delineation and has potential for integration into quantitative disease monitoring and clinical decision-support systems.

title: InterPro: the protein sequence classification resource in 2027.
authors: Matthias Blum; Antonina Andreeva; Sara Chuguransky; Laise Cavalcanti Florentino; Nicole Morveli Flores; Tiago Grego; Emma Elizabeth Mary Hobbs; Beatriz Lazaro Pinto; Alessandro Polignano; Laetitia Meng-Papaxanthos; Felipe Llinares-López; Lucy Colwell; Aron Marchler-Bauer; Nicola Bordin; Alan Bridge; Daniel H Haft; William Klimke; Ivica Letunic; Huaiyu Mi; Darren A Natale; Christine A Orengo; Damiano Piovesan; Catherine Rivoire; Christian J A Sigrist; Paul D Thomas; Silvio C E Tosatto; Cathy H Wu; Alex Bateman
abstract: InterPro (https://www.ebi.ac.uk/interpro) is a freely accessible resource for the classification of protein sequences. It integrates predictive models, known as signatures, from multiple member databases to classify sequences into families and to predict the presence of domains and functionally important sites. The InterPro database provides annotations for hundreds of millions of sequences, ensuring extensive coverage of UniProtKB, the standard repository of protein sequences, and includes mapping to several other major resources, such as Gene Ontology, the Protein Data Bank in Europe (PDBe), and the AlphaFold Protein Structure Database. In this publication we report on the status of InterPro (version 110.0), detailing new developments in the database, its associated web interface, and software. Notable updates include InterPro-N, a deep-learning method that increases sequence coverage of UniProtKB to over 90%; the transition from InterProScan 5 to the completely re-engineered InterProScan 6; the integration of structure-based domain classifications and predicted structures from AlphaFold; a redesigned protein viewer offering a concise summary view; and a new Model Context Protocol (MCP) server that allows AI assistants to query InterPro programmatically. Over the past two years, 9484 new InterPro entries have been created, bringing the total to 54 922. InterPro data, software and tools are freely available.

title: Augmented Fixation of Distal Clavicle Fractures: High Union, Moderate Complications.
authors: Imran Khan; Tahreem Fatima; Kashif Memon; Muhammad Saleem Khan
abstract: Introduction Unstable lateral clavicle fractures (Neer type II) present significant surgical challenges. Combined fixation using a locking clavicular plate and suture-button (e.g., TightRope (Arthrex, Inc., Naples, FL)) augmentation is a biomechanically appealing technique designed to provide both anatomical stability and coracoclavicular (CC) reconstruction. This study reports the early clinical and radiological outcomes of this combined approach in a representative NHS patient cohort. Materials and methods A retrospective case series was conducted of 18 consecutive patients (mean age 48.5 years, 12 males). All patients received a pre-contoured locking plate (Arthrex/Synthes) combined with a suture-button construct for CC augmentation (knotless/knotted TightRope, FiberTape (Arthrex, Inc., Naples, FL) or EndoButton (Smith+Nephew, Watford, UK)). Primary outcomes were radiographic union and complications. Secondary outcomes included range of motion (ROM) and patient-reported outcome measures (PROMs) (Visual Analogue Scale (VAS), QuickDASH, Oxford Shoulder Score). Results Among the 18 patients with documented radiological follow-up, the mean time to union was 23.9 weeks (range 17.4-34.8 weeks). At a mean follow-up of 13.2 months, functional ROM was achieved in 15 patients (84%). Preliminary PROMs from a subset of patients (n = 10) showed a mean Visual Analogue Scale (VAS) pain score of 1.1, mean QuickDASH of 20.1 and mean Oxford Shoulder Score of 52.5. The overall complication rate was 16.7% (3/18), with one patient experiencing two complications. Complications included one implant failure (TightRope construct rupture) requiring revision surgery, one deep wound infection requiring debridement and implant removal, one case of frozen shoulder and one instance of transient neurological symptoms. No cases of plate failure or non-union were observed, although two patients (11.1%) required re-operation (implant removal for infection in one and a planned secondary ligament reconstruction for the failed TightRope construct in the other). Conclusion and significance Combined locking plate and suture-button augmentation for unstable lateral clavicle fractures results in reliable bony union and good early functional outcomes in an NHS setting. While the complication rate reflects the complexity of these injuries and the learning curve associated with the technique, the absence of catastrophic implant failure or non-union is encouraging. This dual-construct technique offers a viable and effective alternative to traditional hook plate fixation.

title: Prediction of Intrinsic Disorder in Protein Sequences Using the Fast and Accurate flDPnn2 Method.
authors: Kui Wang; Gang Hu; Lukasz Kurgan
abstract: Many proteins, particularly in eukaryotes, contain intrinsically disordered regions (IDRs) in their sequences. IDRs lack a stable tertiary structure under physiological conditions, yet they are essential for a broad range of cellular functions. They can be efficiently and accurately identified with computational methods. We focus on flDPnn2, which is an improved version of its predecessor, flDPnn. Results from the recently completed third Critical Assessment of Protein Intrinsic Disorder Prediction (CAID3) show that these improvements led to relatively high prediction accuracy and low runtime, with flDPnn2 taking only 15 s to predict a 1,000-residue-long sequence. Comparative evaluation on CAID3 also revealed that flDPnn2 is the fastest among the most accurate disorder predictors. We provide a practical guide for flDPnn2 users, explaining how to collect and interpret results produced by flDPnn2 via its freely available web server at https://biomine.cs.vcu.edu/servers/flDPnn2/. We also include a case study that provides a helpful illustration for these explanations. The flDPnn2 web server supports batch submission of up to 50 FASTA-formatted protein sequences and provides results in multiple formats, facilitating convenient analysis and interpretation. © 2026 Wiley Periodicals LLC. Basic Protocol 1: Using the flDPnn2 web server to predict protein intrinsic disorder.

title: AI Enabled Automated Digital Image Analysis for Peri-Implant Health Monitoring: A Preliminary Diagnostic Study.
authors: Xinyu Wu; Xindi Wei; Xiaolei Lv; Xiaojiao Fu; Ziqi He; Wanting Yin; Hongchang Lai; Junyu Shi
abstract:
To develop and validate an AI-driven Digital Erythema Score (DES) for objective, non-invasive assessment of peri-implant mucosal erythema using intraoral scan (IOS) data.
An internal dataset (200 patients, 265 implants) was utilized, with the reference standard established via consensus by two independent experts. We developed a U-Net model to automatically segment the peri-implant mucosal margins to calculate the DES and diagnose erythema (modified Gingival Index mGI 0, ≥ 1). We used the YOLO model for object detection to localize erythema regions. The system's diagnostic performance was validated on an independent external dataset (23 patients, 30 implants), supplemented by a multi-observer study to evaluate the AI's assistance across clinicians with varying experience levels.
The U-Net model achieved precise ROI segmentation (Dice similarity coefficient 0.69 ± 0.11) and reliable colorimetric calculation (ICC > 0.95). At the optimal threshold, the DES accurately identified mucosal erythema (AUC, internal 0.9228 [95% CI: 0.8533 to 0.9760], external 0.9018 [0.8135 to 0.9773]). DES and mGI showed significant correlations with bleeding on probing (B = 7.38, OR = 5.32, both p < 0.001). The YOLO model localized inflammatory regions (mAP internal 0.8968, external 0.6820). In the external validation, the DES-driven diagnostic framework enhanced the diagnostic performance of observers with different levels of experience and increased the inter-observer consistency.
The DES provides an objective metric that converts chromatic signals into a diagnostic score and is significantly correlated with clinical inflammation. This AI-driven framework reduces clinical subjectivity and establishes a non-invasive paradigm for teledentistry and high-frequency, home-based monitoring of peri-implant health in the future after validation with patient-accessible imaging devices.
This study has been prospectively registered (NCT07349095).

title: The Role of Artificial Intelligence in Treatment Planning in Physical and Rehabilitation Medicine: A Systematic Review.
authors: Andrea Demeco; Nicola Marotta; Andrea Racinelli; Marco Megna; Bruno Pansera; Stefano Palermi; Marco Vecchiato; Alessandro de Sire; Antonio Ammendolia
journal: American journal of physical medicine & rehabilitation
abstract:
Individualized rehabilitation plans are crucial for maximizing clinical outcomes. Generative artificial intelligence (AI), particularly large language models (LLMs), which can generate new content based on large knowledge bases, could improve personalized rehabilitation. This systematic review aimed to assess accuracy and application of LLMs in rehabilitation.
A systematic search was conducted in PubMed, Web of Science, and Scopus until February 2026. The PICO included LLMs (P), their use in rehabilitation planning (I), comparison with expert opinion or other AI systems (e.g., machine learning, deep learning, or CDSS) (C), the ability to generate appropriate rehabilitation plans and compliance with expert clinicians or clinical practice guidelines (O). Studies involving non-generative AI were excluded. Methodological quality was assessed with JBI tools. Data extraction was performed by two reviewers; a third resolved conflicts.
Nine studies met inclusion criteria. Concordance with expert opinion varied, reaching 98.75% after an expert advisory board reviewed AI-generated statements. In musculoskeletal and cardiovascular rehabilitation, LLMs demonstrated alignment with guidelines. However, the included studies reported hallucinations, underscoring the necessity of supervision.
LLMs showed promising capabilities in supporting rehabilitation treatment planning, possibly offering adaptability and personalization. Nonetheless, high-quality studies are necessary to validate real-world effectiveness and define implementation strategies.

title: An evaluation framework for sparse 4D (3D + time) imaging reconstruction via bootstrapped cross-validation.
authors: Yuhe Zhang; Zisheng Yao; Zhe Hu; Tobias Ritschel; Pablo Villanueva-Perez
abstract: Four-dimensional (4D; 3D + time) microscopic imaging has emerged as a powerful technique for investigating dynamic phenomena in complex systems, enabling direct visualisation of structural evolution in space and time. However, when pushing the limits of spatiotemporal resolution, most time-resolved imaging techniques yield inherently sparse 4D datasets. While deep learning-based reconstruction methods have shown promise in reconstructing 4D from sparse spatiotemporal measurements, a practical approach for evaluating their performance in the absence of a 4D reference has, to the best of our knowledge, been lacking. Here, we present a bootstrapped cross-validation framework that estimates reconstruction performance by quantifying correlations between reconstructions generated from independently sampled subsets of the acquired data, as inspired by the 3D validation strategy in cryo-electron microscopy, where reconstructions from split datasets are compared to assess resolutions. This enables both qualitative and quantitative assessment in the absence of ground truth. We investigate two representative scenarios with sparse and ultra-sparse X-ray datasets and validate this approach using 4D-ONIX, a 4D deep-learning reconstruction method, on simulated water droplet collision experiments. The proposed approach provides a reference-free framework for performance estimation and support for better-informed experimental strategies across a wide range of ultrafast imaging applications.

title: Deep learning-based prediction of insect odorant receptor-ligand interactions for behavioral regulator discovery.
authors: Sibo Wang; Penghao Wang; Aniruddha Agnihotri; Wei Xu; Guirong Wang
abstract:
Widespread chemical insecticide use causes resistance and ecological damage, driving need for sustainable pest control via olfaction-based behavioral regulators targeting odorant receptors (ORs). Conventional screening is costly and low-throughput. Deep learning (DL) offers solutions but faces challenges of scarce data, distinct OR-ligand binding properties, and requirements for explainability to guide regulator design.
To explore effective representations of volatile compounds under a limited data setting, we developed three deep learning models based on molecular descriptors (Concat-Desc), molecular graphs (Concat-GNN), and Simplified Molecular Input Line Entry System (SMILES) sequences (Cross-Attn) for OR-ligand interaction prediction. Trained on 4566 experimental pairs from M2iOR database, all DL models outperformed quantitative structure-activity relationship (QSAR) baselines. Concat-Desc and Cross-Attn achieved superior performance (test area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) = 0.891-0.927; accuracy = 0.810-0.843). The explainability modules highlighted model-associated ligand features and protein sequence positions.
Molecular descriptors and SMILES are effective for volatile compounds in data-limited scenarios, while graph representations require further optimization. Integrated explainability modules provide testable hypotheses for experimental validation and future design, establishing a computational framework for artificial intelligence (AI)-driven insect chemical ecology. Limitations include data scarcity and limited species coverage that future studies must address. © 2026 Society of Chemical Industry.

title: Evaluation of chatbot and specialist knowledge on pediatric sedation and general anesthesia: a comparative analysis.
authors: Dilara Dinç; Aslıhan Ozbilgen
journal: BMC medical informatics and decision making
abstract:
The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) in healthcare has increased rapidly, with large language model-based chatbots emerging as potential tools for education and clinical support. However, their performance in complex medical domains such as sedation and general anesthesia remains underexplored. This study aimed to evaluate the accuracy of AI-supported chatbot models (ChatGPT 4.0 Mini, Gemini 1.5 Pro, and Claude 3 Sonnet) in comparison to human experts (Anesthesiologists, Pediatric Dentists, Oral and Maxillofacial Surgeons) within the context of sedation and general anesthesia.
This descriptive and comparative cross-sectional study utilized a 26-item true/false questionnaire based on ASA, AAP, ADA, and AAPD guidelines. The questionnaire was administered to three chatbots and 72 human participants (24 per specialty). For chatbot evaluation, a zero-shot prompting technique with a uniform command ("Is this statement true or false?") was applied in separate sessions after clearing the cache to ensure standardization. Responses were coded as correct/incorrect by two independent pediatric dentists. Human participants completed the same questionnaire via Google Forms. Descriptive statistics were calculated. Normality of data was assessed using the Shapiro-Wilk test. Non-parametric data were compared using the Kruskal-Wallis test followed by Bonferroni-adjusted post hoc tests. Categorical variables were analyzed using the Pearson Chi-square test. Statistical analyses were performed using IBM SPSS v27.
Significant differences were found among all groups ($p < 0.001$). In terms of text-based guideline retrieval, Claude 3 Sonnet (92.8%) and Gemini 1.5 Pro (91.7%) demonstrated high factual accuracy, while anesthesiologists achieved the highest performance among human clinicians (87.0%). While the chatbot models showed high proficiency in data retrieval for "General Information" and "Postoperative Monitoring," anesthesiologists significantly outperformed the AI models in "Patient Evaluation and Preparation" (91.7%), highlighting a critical gap in AI's clinical reasoning compared to human expertise. Notable knowledge gaps were identified among oral surgeons regarding pharmacological reversal agents.
Claude and Gemini chatbots exhibit high factual accuracy in retrieving guideline-based pediatric sedation theory, suggesting potential exclusively as supplementary informational resources. However, anesthesiologists' superior performance in pre-operative assessment underscores the irreplaceable role of clinical judgment. AI integration should therefore follow a synergistic model, positioning language models strictly as adjunct tools under mandatory human oversight.

title: Multi-task adversarial autoencoder for functional genomic element generation with preserved biophysical properties.
authors: Shamsuddeen Adamu; Hitham Alhussian; Said Jadid Abdulkadir; Majdy Mohamed Eltayeb Eltahir; Sallam O F Khairy; Ibrahim Hayatu Hassan; Ibrahim Muhammad Kurah; Abubakar Mukhtar; Vijayakanthan Ganesalingam; Vaishali Ravi; Yahaya Saidu
abstract: Generative modeling of genomic sequences presents a stringent test for deep learning, requiring the capture of long-range dependencies and functional constraints beyond local nucleotide statistics. Existing architectures frequently collapse to limited modes or reproduce shallow nucleotide distributions without encoding functional semantics. We introduce the Multi-Task Adversarial Autoencoder (MT-AAE), a hybrid generative framework that integrates adversarial regularization with auxiliary functional and biophysical objectives to enforce structured latent representations. Evaluated on an empirical human gene corpus, MT-AAE achieved a Train-on-Synthetic-Test-on-Real (TRTS) accuracy of 74.7%, compared with 41.0% for a standard GAN baseline. Stratified analysis further showed that functional discriminability increased to 89.3% when sequence lengths aligned with the model's architectural window. Importantly, the learned representations exhibited emergent biological structure: synthetic sequences spontaneously preserved cis-regulatory syntax, including canonical TATA-box motifs recovered across 100% of generated promoter sequences without explicit rule encoding, though positional placement relative to the TSS was not statistically significant (KS [Formula: see text]), and the high occurrence rate is partly attributable to the AT-rich composition of the generated sequences. Representation-level validation using frozen DNABERT-2 and DNABERT-S embeddings confirmed that the generated sequences retained functional information beyond shallow k-mer statistics. Cross-species evaluation on Mus musculus sequences further demonstrated species-specific learning consistent with known human-mouse regulatory divergence. The framework also mitigated mode collapse, maintaining near-uniform generation across functional classes ([Formula: see text]), including rare categories such as tRNAs ([Formula: see text] of the dataset). These findings position MT-AAE as an effective framework for biologically constrained genomic sequence generation.

title: Teacher-student-machine interaction autonomous learning: a structured LLM-integrated framework for developing independent clinical reasoning in residency training.
authors: Pengru Wang; He Li; Dingyuan Tu; Huilong Qu; Mengli Chang; Qiying Zhang; Gan Xu; Bo Li; Yingtian Wang; Wei Xu
abstract:
This study evaluated whether a structured pedagogical framework integrating large language models (LLMs) into residency training could develop clinical reasoning competencies that transfer to independent performance.
In this prospective randomized controlled trial, residents were assigned to Teacher-Student-Machine Interaction Autonomous Learning (TSM-AL) group or traditional teaching group. The TSM-AL framework positioned LLMs as supervised cognitive auxiliaries within a five-step case analysis process featuring controlled information release, predefined reasoning tasks, and structured utilization guidelines. Six formative assessments were conducted over 16 weeks, followed by summative examinations under both LLM-assisted and unassisted conditions. Outcomes included clinical reasoning scores, entrustable professional activity (EPA) levels, global faculty ratings, expert-aligned diagnostic accuracy, and standardized patient examination performance.
Significant between-group differences in diagnostic pathway completeness emerged at week 14 (3.53 ± 1.36 vs. 2.68 ± 1.49, P = 0.018) and week 16 (3.35 ± 1.43 vs. 2.37 ± 1.51, P = 0.009). In the unassisted final examination, the TSM-AL group demonstrated significantly higher clinical reasoning scores (7.32 ± 2.30 vs. 5.12 ± 1.66, P < 0.001). EPA distributions differed significantly (P = 0.034), with fewer TSM-AL residents requiring complete supervision (11.76% vs. 29.41%). Global faculty ratings also differed significantly (P = 0.019), with 23.53% of TSM-AL residents achieving Level 5 compared to none in the traditional group. Expert alignment for core problem identification (67.65% vs. 44.12%, P = 0.042) and differential diagnosis matching (73.53% vs. 50.00%, P = 0.046) favored the TSM-AL group. Standardized patient examination scores were significantly higher in the TSM-AL group (80.88 ± 3.82 vs. 78.71 ± 3.90, P = 0.025). Notably, TSM-AL residents performed better without LLM assistance than with assistance.
The TSM-AL framework significantly enhanced clinical reasoning competencies that transferred to independent performance, demonstrating that structured LLM integration develops autonomous reasoning rather than fostering technological dependency.

title: Deep learning-driven classification of 46 medicinal macrofungi species: comparative analysis, fusion strategies, and explainability insights.
authors: Mustafa Sevindik; Aras Fahrettin Korkmaz; Fatih Ekinci; Eda Kumru; Tetiana Krupodorova; Ömer Burak Altindal; Mehmet Serdar Güzel; Ilgaz Akata
abstract: Accurate identification of medicinal and wild macrofungi remains a major challenge due to high intra-species variability, visually overlapping morphologies, and inconsistent field-level imaging conditions. Existing deep learning studies typically focus on limited taxonomic scopes (5-12 classes) and lack systematic comparisons across modern convolutional and transformer architectures, leaving a significant gap in fine-grained fungal classification. This study introduces a comprehensive evaluation framework covering 46 macrofungal species, integrating 18 single backbones and three feature-level fusion strategies under a unified, fully reproducible protocol. All models were trained with identical preprocessing, stratified partitions, deterministic seeds, and a two-stage fine-tuning pipeline to ensure fair architectural comparison. Among single models, ConvNeXt-Base achieved the strongest performance with 96.59% accuracy, 0.966 macro-F1, 0.965 MCC, 0.9997 macro-AUC, and 0.1054 log-loss, exhibiting a near-diagonal confusion matrix where 25 classes reached perfect recall. Although feature-level fusion did not exceed the best single model in overall accuracy, it improved stability for several visually difficult taxa. The best ensemble, ConvNeXt-Base + DeiT-Base, achieved 95.85% accuracy, 0.958 macro-F1, and 0.9995 macro-AUC, remaining close to the ConvNeXt-Base baseline while providing complementary class-level robustness. The reported latency of ≈0.0021 s/image refers only to the precomputed-feature mode, in which backbone features are already cached and only the shared MLP head is evaluated. Therefore, this value should not be interpreted as full end-to-end inference latency for newly acquired field images. Explainability analyses using Grad-CAM and Integrated Gradients demonstrated that both single and fused models rely on biologically meaningful structures such as gill edges, pore surfaces, cap margins, and hymenophore textures. Overall, this study provides one of the most extensive quantitative benchmarks for macrofungal recognition to date and establishes a reproducible, architecture-agnostic foundation for future multimodal, large-scale, and explainable AI systems in fungal taxonomy.

title: Vibrational spectroscopy of microorganisms: A review.
authors: Cushla McGoverin
abstract: Vibrational spectroscopic methods, mid- and near-infrared, and Raman spectroscopies, have been extensively applied to the study of microorganisms. This is due to the relatively rapid analysis time, relative low-cost, experimental flexibility, and phenotypic nature of these methods. Consequently, vibrational spectroscopies have been investigated for clinical, environmental and industrial microbiology applications. This review outlines the principles of mid- and near-infrared, and Raman spectroscopies, and steps through vibrational spectroscopic experiments in the context of microbiological studies. Further applications within species/strain identification, antimicrobial resistance, bioremediation, cell sorting and intracellular microbial protein analysis are examined. Vibrational spectroscopy is expected to become increasingly routine in microbial analyses, particularly in clinical settings, driven by the harmonisation of spectral databases, the expanding application of deep learning methods and improved instrumentation to reduce sampling-to-reporting time.

title: Multiscale adaptive graph attention band selection for hyperspectral rosewood species classification.
authors: Shuo Xu; Hang Su; Changwei Gu; Lei Zhao
abstract:
The identification of precious timber represented by national standard Rosewood remains challenged by the time-intensive and destructive nature of conventional approaches. Hyperspectral imaging offers a non-destructive alternative, yet its application is hindered by high dimensionality and spectral redundancy. Existing methods often struggle to simultaneously capture global spectral dependencies and localized chemical features. This study presents an integrated framework combining a multiscale adaptive graph attention-based band selection method with stability consistency (MAGABSS-SC) and a dual-domain resonant state space network (D2R-S2Net). MAGABSS-SC employs supervised multiscale attention and PageRank propagation to identify topologically robust bands, which are directly fed into D2R-S2Net to integrate frequency-domain filtering with temporal state space sequence modeling.
Evaluated on a hyperspectral dataset of eighteen Rosewood species comprising 1800 spectral samples, D2R-S2Net achieved an accuracy of 93.33% using full-band input, outperforming support vector machines, random forests, and one-dimensional vision transformers. When combined with MAGABSS-SC, the classification accuracy reached 95.93% while retaining 80% of the spectral bands. The selected wavelengths exhibited contiguous cluster distributions aligned with general absorption intervals reported in wood spectroscopy literature.
The proposed framework provides an accurate and non-destructive approach for the classification of endangered rosewood species. By mitigating spectral redundancy and noise interference, it demonstrates the feasibility of combining graph-based band selection with dual-domain deep learning for timber identification and forest resource regulation.

title: Practical Solutions to Common TAVI Complications
authors: Herbert Kroon
abstract: Aortic valve stenosis Calcific aortic valve degeneration mainly affects the elderly population. Approximately 15% of elderly patients have some degree of aortic stenosis (AS)1. Untreated severe AS will lead to heart failure, angina and/or syncope and approximately half of patients will expire within 2 years after symptom onset1, 2. Historically, open heart surgery was the only treatment for severe AS. However, advanced age was a dominant argument to defer surgery. Transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) was contrived as a less invasive alternative to surgery and to fulfill this unmet clinical need. After the first-in-human procedure in 2002, TAVI matured into a guideline recommended treatment of symptomatic severe AS in elderly patients across the entire risk spectrum3-7. Peri-procedural embolization Operator experience, improved planning and implantation strategies and multiple device iterations including smaller profile, repositioning ability and outer sealing fabric converted TAVI into a reproducible and relatively safe procedure8. However, the “Big Five” of complications in the modern TAVI era remain 1) access site complications and bleedings, 2) paravalvular leakage (PVL), 3) acute kidney injury (AKI), 4) conduction disturbances including the need for permanent pacemaker implantation (PPI) and 5) stroke9. Up to 5% of patients suffer a neurological event after TAVI, mainly within the first 48 hours8, 10, 11. This finding suggests a direct causative role with the transcatheter valve implantation itself. Transcranial Doppler and brain Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) studies revealed debris embolization towards the brain and new brain lesions after TAVI in the vast majority of patients12-15. Most of these embolizations remain clinically silent at first sight but may be linked to neurocognitive decline and frank dementia16. Embolic protection devices (EPD) have been developed to deflect or capture embolized debris on its way to the brain and may possibly reduce brain lesions and neurological events including stroke and neurocognitive decline. Part I of this thesis adds perspective to the etiopathology of TAVI related stroke and the mechanism of action of the current spectrum of cerebral embolic protection devices. We also present insights into the microscopic analysis of debris that was captured with filters during TAVI procedures. Vascular access and complications 1 TAVI typically requires large bore femoral artery access. By default, larger arteriotomies are at higher risk for access site complications and bleedings. A completely percutaneous approach relies on vascular access closure devices (VCD) to manage the arteriotomy and provide patent hemostasis. TAVI in low to intermediate risk patients is associated with a major vascular complication rate ranging between 2 and 8%4, 11. The conventional closure technique is based on sutures and most access site complications after TAVI procedures are related to closure device failure17. A collagen plug based closure device was introduced as an alternative to sutures. Part II of this thesis addresses vascular complications and provides information on clinical outcomes with collagen plug-based VCD. TAVI-related conduction disturbances Acquired conduction disturbances after TAVI are frequent and may lead to heart failure (re-) admissions and impaired long-term prognosis18-22. The atrioventricular bundle pierces the membranous septum between the right and non-coronary cusp of the aortic valve and surfaces along the left ventricular outflow tract (LVOT), which makes it vulnerable to contact pressure by the implanted transcatheter heart valve (THV) during TAVI23, 24. New left bundle branch block (LBBB) and third-degree atrioventricular block (AV3B) requiring PPI occur in up to a third and quarter of patients, respectively18-22. These conduction disturbances may be transient or remain permanent which is clinically relevant in view of in-hospital stay and overall healthcare costs. Unfortunately, there are no uniform definitions to describe conduction dynamics post-TAVI. Inconsistent reporting makes the interpretation of the literature on this topic challenging. Part III of this thesis will elaborate on what is currently known about the incidence of newly acquired conduction disturbances after TAVI and studies specific features on the baseline and postprocedural electrocardiogram (ECG) to predict conduction dynamics. These insights may help determine the need and timing of PPI and adjust hospital discharge policies.

title: AORTIC DILATATION AS A CLUE TO BICUSPID AORTIC VALVE FROM DIAGNOSIS TO TIMELY SURGERY A CASE REPORT AND LITERATURE REVIEW
authors: N. Annane² Z. Bennoui*¹
journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: Background: Bicuspid aortic valve (BAV) may be associated with progressive aortic enlargement despite preserved valve function. Selecting the appropriate time for prophylactic intervention requires aortic phenotyping and individualized risk assessment. Case presentation: A 56-year-old man without significant medical history or cardiovascular risk factors was evaluated before surgery for lumbar disc herniation with motor-deficit sciatica. He was asymptomatic from a cardiac standpoint; examination revealed no aortic murmur, blood pressure was 120/70 mmHg, and ECG showed sinus rhythm at 75 beats/min without left ventricular hypertrophy. Chest radiography suggested proximal aortic enlargement. Echocardiography revealed type 0 BAV with morphologically altered cusps but neither stenosis nor regurgitation, and an aortic diameter of 42 mm at both the sinuses of Valsalva and sinotubular junction. Cardiac chambers were normal, and laboratory assessment was unremarkable. Discussion: BAV-related aortopathy requires evaluation independently of valve dysfunction. Current US and European guidance generally supports imaging surveillance at 42 mm rather than prophylactic surgery, in the absence of additional high-risk findings. Conclusion: Comprehensive aortic imaging, familial assessment, and lifelong surveillance are central to management of incidentally identified BAV aortopathy.

title: Trends in rheumatic heart disease mortality in the United States of America from 1968 to 2023: a nationwide analysis
authors: Jacky H. K. Chen; Dean Nelson; Adam Trytell; Andrew Burns; Noel Bayley; Elizabeth Davida Paratz
abstract: Abstract Background Rheumatic heart disease (RHD) is a preventable sequela of acute rheumatic fever causing chronic valvular damage to the heart. In the United States of America (USA), RHD persists among socioeconomically disadvantaged populations. This study examines long-term trends in RHD mortality from 1968 to 2023, identifying associated demographic and geographic factors to guide targeted public health interventions. Methods This retrospective observational study examined death certificate data from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention’s Wide-Ranging Online Data for Epidemiologic Research (WONDER) database, encompassing three different International Classification of Disease periods (ICD-8, ICD-9, ICD-10). Analysis included stratification by age, gender, race, ethnicity and urbanisation level. Joinpoint analysis and multiple regression analysis were used to identify trends. Results RHD mortality declined significantly from 1968 to 2012, with falling crude mortality rates in both sexes and large reductions in absolute deaths among White individuals and adults aged 55–74 years. From 2012 to 2023, total deaths increased from 3,083 to 4,332, crude mortality rose from 0.98 to 1.29 per 100,000 and age-adjusted mortality increased from 0.88 to 1.04 per 100,000 (all p < 0.0001). Increases were observed across sex, race, ethnicity, urbanisation, and most age subgroups. Females had consistently higher RHD crude mortality rate ratios than men (1.09–2.43). The age distribution of RHD mortality shifted markedly over the study period, with deaths among individuals aged ≥ 75 years increasing from 17% in 1968 to 61% in 2023. Race- and ethnicity-specific CMR increased across all assessed groups from 2012 to 2023, with the largest relative increases among American Indian or Alaska Native individuals (+ 112.4%; β = 0.033 per 100,000/year, p = 0.002) and Hispanic individuals (+ 60.2%; β = 0.014 per 100,000/year, p < 0.001). Conclusion Following decades of decline, RHD mortality in the United States increased after 2012. Our study identified a persistent female predominance in RHD mortality and a marked shift in mortality burden from middle-aged adults towards older populations.

title: Comparison of general anesthesia and spinal anesthesia in patients with moderate to severe aortic stenosis undergoing surgery for hip fracture: a retrospective cohort study
authors: Tomoyo Ando; Nobuko Fujita; Yuki Yonekura; K Miyasaka; Seiki Abe
abstract: Abstract Background: Patients with moderate to severe aortic stenosis undergoing hip fracture surgery are at high risk for perioperative complications, but data comparing spinal anesthesia and general anesthesia are limited. Historically, spinal anesthesia has been considered relatively contraindicated in patients with aortic stenosis, but there is no clear evidence supporting this assumption. Methods: We conducted a single-center retrospective observational study of patients with moderate to severe aortic stenosis undergoing hip fracture surgery. Patients were classified by anesthetic technique (general anesthesia or spinal anesthesia). The primary outcome was intraoperative hypotension, quantified as the area under the threshold, representing the duration and magnitude of mean arterial pressure below 65 mmHg. Secondary outcomes included the ratio of hypotensive time to total anesthesia time, vasopressor requirements, 30-day mortality, postoperative complications, time to first analgesic request, and numeric rating scale pain scores postoperatively. Results: Among 103 patients analyzed (general anesthesia = 76; spinal anesthesia = 27), baseline characteristics were comparable between groups. Spinal anesthesia was associated with lower area under the threshold for mean arterial pressure below 65 mmHg (β = -260 mmHg·min, 95% CI, -470 to -43; p = 0.019), smaller hypotension ratio (β = -9.8%, 95% CI, -20 to -0.042; p = 0.049), and reduced phenylephrine use (β = -1.6 mg, 95% CI, -2.3 to -0.96; p < 0.01). There were no statistical differences between groups in mortality and postoperative complications (30-day mortality: OR 0.52, 95% CI, 0.033 to 8.1; p = 0.64; acute kidney injury: OR 1.2, 95% CI, 0.46 to 3.4, p = 0.68; delirium: OR 0.48, 95% CI, 0.19 to 1.2; p = 0.13; heart failure: OR 1.4, 95% CI, 0.41 to 4.7; p = 0.59). Conclusions: In patients with moderate to severe aortic stenosis undergoing hip fracture surgery, spinal anesthesia significantly reduced intraoperative hypotension and vasopressor use, compared with general anesthesia. These findings suggest that spinal anesthesia may be a safe and practical alternative to general anesthesia in patients with moderate to severe aortic stenosis.

title: Pre-transplant cardiovascular risks and adverse outcomes in patients after receiving kidney transplantation
authors: XIN WAN; Zhihong Xu; 魏仁善; Huogen Liu; Ling Gu; YUNDI SHI; Yanzhou Zhu; Xi Zeng
abstract: Kidney transplantation (KT) has been reported to significantly improve the survival rate of patients with end-stage renal disease, but the long-term risk for major adverse cardiovascular and cerebrovascular events (MACCE) or mortality remains uncertain. Our study aimed to evaluate the association between cardiovascular risk factors and adverse outcomes in patients after KT. Using raw data from the National Health Insurance Research Database in Taiwan, we included 3,562 adult patients (1997–2013) who underwent uncomplicated KT. The median follow-up was 7.7 years (IQR 4.8–10.6), with a total of 28,267 person-years. Patients were censored at the date of the primary event, death, or December 31, 2013, whichever occurred first. We evaluated adverse outcomes, including non-fatal acute myocardial infarction (AMI), non-fatal stroke, and/or all-cause death, as primary events during the observation period (up to 17 years). The association of cardiovascular risk factors before KT was assessed using multivariate Cox proportional hazards models, adjusted for age, sex, and other available baseline factors. We also performed Kaplan–Meier analysis to estimate the cumulative risk. Among these patients, 225 (6.3%) were aged over 60 years, and 1,895 (53.2%) were male. All-cause death occurred in 703 patients (19.7%), non-fatal AMI in 125 (3.5%), and non-fatal stroke in 104 (2.9%). Only 853 patients (23.9%) had a waiting time for KT of < 1 year. Logistic regression analysis showed that only diabetes (OR = 2.085, 95% CI: 1.749–2.484, P < 0.001), AMI (OR = 2.568, 95% CI: 1.621–4.070, P < 0.001), and stroke before KT (OR = 4.376, 95% CI: 2.720–7.041, P < 0.001) were significantly associated with primary events, whereas hypertension and dyslipidemia were not. Consistently, the fully adjusted Cox model showed that diabetes (HR = 1.560, 95% CI: 1.338–1.819, P < 0.001), AMI (HR = 1.692, 95% CI: 1.188–2.410, P = 0.004), and stroke before KT (HR = 2.226, 95% CI: 1.612–3.074, P < 0.001) were independently associated with the composite primary event. Pre-transplant diabetes, AMI, and stroke were associated with increased risks of MACCE and all-cause mortality after KT. These findings support preoperative cardiovascular risk stratification in KT candidates.

title: Myocardial remodelling during sacubitril/valsartan therapy in patients with chronic heart failure.
authors: DAVID TABUKASHVILI; V. Kapetivadze; Tamar Lazashvili; Zviadi Maglaperidze
abstract: Abstract: The aim of the study was to identify differences between aliskiren and sacubitril/valsartan in their ability to influence cardiac remodelling, metabolic balance, neurohumoral activation, and clinical symptom severity. A comparative assessment of the clinical effectiveness and impact on the structural and functional state of the myocardium was conducted for two therapeutic strategies in patients with chronic heart failure in Georgia over a 12-month follow-up. The results demonstrated fundamentally different trajectories of therapeutic response. In the sacubitril/valsartan group, early clinical improvement was observed by 6 months, including significant reductions in systolic blood pressure (-6.2%, p<0.001), respiratory rate (-4.5%, p<0.001), and N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide levels (-10.0%, p<0.05), along with improved oxygen saturation (+3.5%, p<0.001). Left ventricular ejection fraction increased significantly already at 6 months (from 34.2±4.7% to 37.4±4.0%, p<0.001) and further at 12 months (40.5±3.5%, p<0.001), accompanied by rapid improvement in New York Heart Association functional class, with 9.3% of patients achieving New York Heart Association I by study end. In contrast, the aliskiren group exhibited slower but more pronounced structural reverse remodelling. Significant reductions in left ventricular end-systolic volume (-15.8%, p=0.009), end-diastolic volume (-17.6%, p=0.016), and end-systolic diameter (p=0.002) were observed only at 12 months, along with a modest but significant increase in ejection fraction (p=0.030). Regression of functional mitral and tricuspid regurgitation and a significant decrease in pulmonary artery systolic pressure (-19.7%, p<0.05) were more prominent in this group. Both therapies led to significant improvements in carbohydrate and lipid metabolism, including reductions in glycated haemoglobin, low-density lipoprotein cholesterol, and triglycerides (p<0.05 for all), indicating a favourable systemic metabolic effect. Overall, findings suggest that sacubitril/valsartan may be preferable when rapid clinical stabilization is required, whereas aliskiren may represent an effective therapeutic option for patients with advanced structural cardiac remodelling.

title: Atrial Distensibility Predicts Short-Term Prognosis in Fetal Single Ventricle-Type Congenital Heart Disease with Atrioventricular Valve Regurgitation
authors: Yohei Akazawa; Kosuke Yonehara; Haruka Obinata; Ryusuke Numata; Yuma Shibuya; Kohta Takei; Kiyohiro Takigiku
abstract: Abstract We aimed to determine whether the assessment of atrial distensibility helps predict perinatal outcomes in fetuses with a prenatal diagnosis of single ventricle-type congenital heart disease (SVCHD) with atrioventricular valve regurgitation (AVVR). We retrospectively identified 77 consecutive cases of fetuses with SVCHD examined between 2011 and 2023. Atrial distensibility and conventional echocardiographic parameters used to assess the severity of fetal heart failure were measured retrospectively. Fetuses with SVCHD were divided into two groups according to AVVR severity: no-mild or ≥moderate. The primary endpoint was the occurrence of composite adverse events (fetal demise, neonatal death of any cause, and early infantile valvuloplasty). The impact of atrial distensibility on prognosis was assessed using the receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis. Overall, 77 fetuses were diagnosed prenatally with SVCHD; 9 were terminated, and 8 were excluded due to chromosomal abnormalities. Of the 60 fetuses with SVCHD, 48 and 12 had no-mild and ≥moderate AVVR, respectively. Atrial distensibility was significantly lower in fetuses with SVCHD and ≥moderate AVVR than in those with no-mild AVVR (p < 0.001). Among fetuses with SVCHD and ≥moderate AVVR, atrial distensibility was impaired in fetuses with adverse events compared to those without adverse events (p < 0.05). ROC analysis indicated that atrial distensibility exhibited a significant predictive value for composite adverse outcomes in fetal SVCHD with ≥moderate AVVR (area under the curve 0.90; p = 0.02). Quantitative assessment of atrial distensibility may have clinical utility in predicting the perinatal outcomes of fetal SVCHD with significant AVVR.
